properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 5:48AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected to occur.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Colorado, including the
following areas, the Eastern San Juan Mountains, and the Upper Rio
Grande Valley.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.
Rockslides will be possible in the mountainous areas. Highway 160
and Highway 17 will likely be significantly impacted by this storm.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rainfall is expected to fall Sunday and Monday across the
area, leading to elevated concerns for flooding in areas that
have recently received excessive moisture, or have recently
experienced flooding.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the Rio Grande, including Del Norte and Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 1:13AM MST until November 2 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall over saturated
soils.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...From 11 PM MST Saturday through 5 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A second round of rain and isolated thunderstorms is expected
Saturday night through the early morning hours of Monday. An
additional 1 to 3 inches of rain will be possible, on already
saturated ground.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

Consider changing your plans if you were going to hike, boat, or
paddleboard to a slot canyon or normally dry wash. If you do still
decide to recreate, check in at a nearby visitor center or ranger
station.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 1:38AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northwest, and west central New
Mexico, including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,
Far Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands and
Tusas Mountains Including Chama. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska
Mountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico, San
Francisco River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central
Highlands, West Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of widespread rainfall is expected Sunday into
Monday with rainfall amounts generally between 1 and 2 inches
near and west of the Continental Divide, except near 3 inches in
favored upslope regions of the Tusas Mountains near Chama. This
rainfall will occur over very saturated soils which will increase
runoff. These are also areas that are still recovering from the
last flood event. River rises are likely, but rises are not
expected to be as high as the last flood event. If river flooding
materializes, it will likely continue into Monday evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 30 at 9:40PM MDT until November 1 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef
National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake
Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread moderate to at times heavy precipitation is expected
across much of southern, southeast and east central Utah
beginning late Saturday night, and continuing throughout the day
Sunday.

Moist antecedent conditions from recent heavy rains will result
in efficient and excessive runoff, allowing all area washes,
streams and rivers to run fast and high. Flood prone areas will
likely become inundated at times, and backcountry roads will
likely become impassable from this excessive runoff.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
